content:
sam (customer): Hey team — our EOD authorization batch kicked off ~00:00 UTC and we're getting a flood of 429s. Noticed it spikes right after token refreshes run. Sample error: 
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{ "error": "Rate limit exceeded" }

maya (support): Sorry you're hitting this, we can help triage. Can you paste the response headers (X-RateLimit-*) and a couple of request IDs? Also: are those token refreshes creating many simultaneous clients?

sam (customer): Headers from one failing response: 
X-RateLimit-Limit: 3600 (per hour)
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 45
X-Request-Id: req_0a7b9c

We run an EOD process that spins up 500 workers and each refreshes tokens at start, so likely a stampede.

maya (support): That matches a classic token-refresh stampede hitting the per-tenant throttle. Immediate mitigations: pause the job, stagger startup, or temporarily reduce concurrency. We'll also check if we can provide a short burst increase while you patch client.

alex (eng): Quick note: gateway enforces both per-key and per-tenant windows (RPM/TPM). If it's token refresh fanout, tokens being requested in parallel will multiply requests. We can do a temporary tenant quota bump but need customer_id and target window/time. I'll open an internal change.

jin (sre): Can you repro in staging with smaller scale? Also check auth service logs for many token issuance events at the same timestamp — that will confirm the stampede. We have a replay tool (replay-bot) you can use to re-run the job with pacing.

sam (customer): Request ID examples: req_0a7b9c, req_0a7b9d, req_0a7b9f. Quick repro script we used (bash):
```
TOKEN=$(curl -s https://auth.example.com/get-token | jq -r .access_token)
for i in {1..500}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/authz &
done
wait
```
That snippet is what the batch manager does on startup (we know it's naive).

maya (support): Thanks — that shows the pattern. Recommendations:
- change client to shared token acquisition (one refresh per group) or add a small randomized jitter on startup.
- add exponential backoff when receiving 429 and respect Retry-After header.
- if you must start many workers, warm tokens gradually (ramp).

alex (eng): I've opened INC-1725 and assigned to eng-runtime. I can approve a temporary tenant quota bump for 30 minutes to let you finish the EOD run if you want. We need the customer_id and the time window you want the bump to apply.

sam (customer): Please apply a 30-minute bump starting 00:05 UTC to cover the run. Customer id is cust_42. We'll also push a quick client change to pool refreshes and add jitter.

jin (sre): I'll standby to watch the gateway metrics during the window. If we see sustained errors after the bump, we'll roll back and throttle at the gateway to protect other tenants.

maya (support): Handoff: support -> eng-runtime for quota bump (INC-1725). Support will monitor with you during the window. Also filing a short postmortem template for the client change so we can prevent repeat. :thumbsup:

sam (customer): Thanks everyone, implementing token pooling now and will report back once run completes.

replay-bot: To replay safely, use: `replay-bot --tenant cust_42 --concurrency 50 --ramp 5m` — this will simulate paced startup instead of a stampede.

maya (support): Closing support thread and moving to eng for quota action. Keep us tagged on any followup.
